Jordan / Neha —

Thanks for the flag. Quick summary for the customer-facing doc (I also attached a polished PDF draft):

1) What happened (plain language): Between 02:14–02:43 UTC on 2027-01-14, a concurrent autoscaler window mis-evaluated idle workers which temporarily reduced available inference capacity supporting synchronous short-sequence calls. That capacity drop caused our gateway to respond with 429s for a subset of clients with bursty checkout patterns.

2) Root cause (technical): An edge case in the autoscaler’s cooldown logic allowed parallel scale-down operations when a transient spike in CPU utilization coincided with a scheduled job. The parallel scale-down path did not re-check the global worker pool before removing instances. This is fixed in the autoscaler code (PR: #4872) and will be included in the next deploy.

3) Mitigation during event: At 02:43 UTC the on-call engineer forced a scale-up to restore worker pool and enabled a temporary soft-limit on concurrent requests for impacted routes to preserve throughput. Latency normalized immediately and 429s dropped to baseline within ~5 minutes.

4) Action items and timelines (customer-facing commitments):
- Short term (completed within 48 hrs): tightened the autoscaler lock to prevent parallel scale-downs (deployed 2027-01-16), and added an automated rollback if healthy capacity drops >20% in 10s.
- Medium term (30 days): enhanced monitoring and alerts for rapid capacity drops, plus a simulation test added to the CI that exercises concurrent scale events.
- Long term (90 days): improved routing fallbacks so compatible model variants can be used automatically when capacity is constrained.

5) Recommended customer actions: No configuration changes required; if Astra wants stricter SLA guarantees we can schedule a dedicated capacity discussion.

I attached the customer PDF (rca-final.pdf) and the timeline CSV for their ops team. Neha — can you confirm the exact deploy IDs and the monitor thresholds so I can include them in the appendix?

Grace O'Connor
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
